domain_hypothesis.reasoning: The dataset contains explicit columns detailing employee demographics, role identifiers, satisfaction metrics, performance indicators, and attrition, which are classic characteristics of an HR workforce analytics database.

kpi_specs.name: Overall Attrition Rate
kpi_specs.description: Calculates the overall percentage of employees who have left the organization.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT ROUND((SUM(CASE WHEN Attrition = 'Yes' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) * 100.0) / COUNT(*), 2) AS attrition_rate FROM data
kpi_specs.reasoning: This is the primary high-level metric for retention tracking, naturally displayed as a single key summary card.

kpi_specs.name: Attrition Count and Headcount by Department
kpi_specs.description: Compares employee attrition count against total headcount within each department.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT Department, SUM(CASE WHEN Attrition = 'Yes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS attrition_count, COUNT(*) AS total_employees FROM data GROUP BY Department ORDER BY attrition_count DESC
kpi_specs.reasoning: A bar chart allows easy visual comparison of churn volumes across the company's operational departments.

kpi_specs.name: Compensation and Hike Breakdown by Job Role
kpi_specs.description: Provides a comprehensive table of average monthly income and salary hike percentage grouped by job roles.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT JobRole, COUNT(*) AS employee_count, ROUND(AVG(MonthlyIncome), 2) AS avg_monthly_income, ROUND(AVG(PercentSalaryHike), 2) AS avg_salary_hike_pct FROM data GROUP BY JobRole ORDER BY avg_monthly_income DESC
kpi_specs.reasoning: A table is highly effective for detailed multi-column comparisons and rankings across many distinct job categories.

kpi_specs.name: Attrition Rate by Overtime Status
kpi_specs.description: Evaluates if working overtime correlates with higher attrition rates.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT OverTime, ROUND((SUM(CASE WHEN Attrition = 'Yes' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) / COUNT(*)) * 100, 2) AS attrition_rate FROM data GROUP BY OverTime
kpi_specs.reasoning: Comparing the categorical OverTime column (Yes vs No) against Attrition Rate is best represented using a clear comparative bar chart.

kpi_specs.name: Attrition Rate Trend by Tenure
kpi_specs.description: Displays how the attrition rate behaves relative to the number of years an employee has worked at the company.
kpi_specs.sql_query: SELECT YearsAtCompany, ROUND((SUM(CASE WHEN Attrition = 'Yes' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) / COUNT(*)) * 100, 2) AS attrition_rate FROM data GROUP BY YearsAtCompany ORDER BY YearsAtCompany ASC
kpi_specs.reasoning: Tenure (Years at Company) behaves as a sequential numeric progression. A line chart reveals trends, showing if attrition spikes during early tenure stages.
